source_note: Compiled from the Consortium of National Law Universities' official UG syllabus page (consortiumofnlus.ac.in) as reported by multiple 2025-2026 coaching/exam-tracker sources (PhysicsWallah, Careers360, iQuanta, CollegeDekho, CLATapult), cross-checked Sep 2026. CLAT moved to an all-passage-based format from 2020 onward and further trimmed question count to 120 from CLAT 2024 onward (down from 150, and 200 pre-2020) — there are no standalone factual-recall questions left in any section except the data given inside Quantitative Techniques caselets. Always verify against the current-year Consortium notification before finalising a question bank, since the exact section-wise question range can shift slightly year to year within the declared bands.
exam_pattern_note: CLAT UG 2026: 120 single-correct MCQs, 120 minutes, offline pen-and-paper mode, no sectional time limits. Every section except part of Quantitative Techniques is passage-based (English ~450-500 word passages; Current Affairs/GK passages; Legal Reasoning fact-pattern + legal-principle passages; Logical Reasoning ~450-word argumentative passages). There is no separate essay, interview, or numerical-value component.

sections.question_format: Reading-comprehension passages (450-500 words) with attached MCQs, plus standalone vocabulary/grammar-in-context items drawn from within or alongside a passage.

subtopics: Main idea / primary purpose of the passage
Vocabulary in context (contextual meaning of words/phrases used in the passage)
Author's tone, viewpoint and argument structure
Common grammatical error spotting within a passage-linked context

sections.question_format: Short passages/excerpts (often drawn from news reports, journalistic writing, or non-fiction) on current or recent events, followed by MCQs testing comprehension plus factual/background knowledge needed to fully understand the passage.

subtopics: Recent national and international news of significance
Government schemes, policies and economic developments
Historical events referenced in a contemporary context
Polity and constitutional developments in the news

sections.question_format: 4-6 passages presenting a legal principle/rule (real or hypothetical) plus a fact situation; candidates apply the stated principle to the facts. No prior legal knowledge is formally assumed, but familiarity with core legal doctrines materially helps.

subtopics: Basic structure and organs of the Constitution
Offer and acceptance, consideration, capacity to contract
Current legal developments and legal current affairs

sections.question_format: Short argumentative passages of about 450 words, each followed by one or more MCQs. No standalone puzzle, syllogism or blood-relation questions since the 2020 all-passage-based revamp; everything is argument-analysis based.

subtopics: Recognising an argument, its premises and conclusion
Identifying the structure of reasoning in a passage
Strengthen / weaken the argument based on altered premises or facts
Inferring what follows from the passage
Assessing the overall effectiveness of an argument

sections.question_format: Short sets of facts/propositions, graphs, or other textual/pictorial representations of numerical data ('caselets'), each followed by a series of MCQs. Mathematical content is capped at roughly Class 10 level.

subtopics: Reading and deriving information from tables, bar/line/pie charts
Reading pictorial or diagrammatic representations of data
Applying arithmetic operations to the derived data to answer a linked series of questions
